sources.title: CPPItertools range and enumerate
sources.version_or_date: live C++17-targeted README; linked source license copyright 2013
sources.sections_read: README range, enumerate, and lifetime discussion
sources.confirmed: The library documents start/stop/step ranges, descending values, index-element iteration, and range indexing; zero stride yields an empty range. Its current interface targets C++17.
sources.limits: This C++17 library is later evidence, its zero-step range is empty rather than an error, and its binding and lifetime rules cannot be copied into dynamic Python unchanged. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C09.json.

sources.title: more-itertools numeric_range and islice_extended
sources.version_or_date: more-itertools 11.2.1; history includes post-2025 changes and copyright 2012
sources.confirmed: numeric_range accepts start, stop, and step, supports negative steps, and rejects zero; islice_extended applies start/stop/step selection to iterables with negative components supported.
sources.limits: Ordinary callable names remain rebindable; negative slicing may need buffering, generic numeric arithmetic can have precision concerns, and these APIs do not by themselves settle mutation-during-iteration semantics. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C09.json.

sources.title: Cython typed integer-loop lowering
sources.version_or_date: Cython live repository/documentation; Language Basics version 3.4.0a0, copyright 2026
sources.confirmed: The compiler lowers range loops with a C integer induction variable; it also documents an older relational for-from syntax with stride and warns that this syntax is deprecated. Integer overflow constrains optimization.
sources.limits: This is a later compiler with explicit C types; overflow timing can change, its relational for-from syntax is deprecated, and the inspected documentation does not prove that arbitrary redefinition of Python builtins is preserved. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C09.json.

sources.title: Iterate numerical drivers and inline macro expansion
sources.version_or_date: current Iterate manual adaptation; manual credits 1989 original and 2006 adaptation
sources.confirmed: The numerical driver specifies start, inclusive or exclusive bound, direction, and positive stride magnitude; descending direction is separate from stride sign.
sources.limits: Its macro system and code walking do not transfer directly to Python; downward iteration uses a positive stride magnitude, and changing runtime bindings cannot silently inherit macro expansion semantics. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C09.json.
